HYPOCHLORHYDRIA
Diminished gastric acid allows increased numbers of bacteria in the stomach and
predisposes to infection with several potentially pathogenic bacterial species.

These changes increase the risk of nosocomial pneumonia and possibly the risk of
community-acquired respiratory infections.  However, interventions to
decontaminate the upper gastrointestinal tract do not prevent infectious
disease.
